Correctness holds for buffered case only.

GZIP compressed_body_only_discrimination reported as 0.059/0.071 (JSON), 0.048/0.067 (HTML), 0.088/0.054 (XML) while BROTLI-MC compressed is 0.5 for same bodies and decompressed is 0.5 for all gzip cells. Independent local recomputation using identical BODY_GENERATORS and gzip.compress default (mtime=0) + brotli quality6 yields compressed discrimination 0.5 for BOTH encodings (valid vs error hashes distinct: JSON gzip e8a2aecc vs 78ef7592, HTML 4369f1b7 vs bc63cc8c, XML 8d022707 vs 48b4398e). Producer interprets low gzip value as higher compression ratio; local test falsifies that interpretation. Anomaly does not affect C1/C2 falsifier (decompression correctness 1.0 and silent_fallback 0 verified) or C_NULL_CONTROL, but indicates measurement or reporting error in compressed discrimination metric for gzip cells. Decision rule does not depend on this metric.

validity_findings.finding: Validity_notes and spec claim gzip 1KB payloads compress to 300-600 bytes spanning 10-19 chunks at 32 bytes. Local recomputation shows actual compressed sizes at 1KB: JSON 95/107 bytes (3-4 chunks), HTML 229/233 bytes (7-8 chunks), XML 211/220 bytes (7 chunks); brotli 70/83, 172/173, 161/165 bytes (3-6 chunks). Stress is 3-8 chunks, not 10-19. Chunk-boundary test is still valid (multi-chunk vs single-chunk 1024 both 1.0) but weaker than described. Larger payloads (10KB/100KB) needed to test 100+ chunk stress remains unresolved and correctly excluded from ceiling.

validity_findings.finding: decompress_body tries brotli first then gzip up to max_depth=5 per iteration. For gzip payloads first brotli attempt fails (exception) then gzip succeeds depth 1; for brotli first succeeds; for IDENTITY both fail and returns raw unchanged. No multi-layer encoding tested (max_depth>1 never exercised). Depth 5 is generous for gzip->identity. Silent fallback detection SHA256(decompressed)==SHA256(raw) when CE in {gzip,br} correctly classifies failure to decompress. Decompression_altered raw!=decompressed for all 240 gzip +120 brotli observations (10/10 per state) proves pipeline actually decompressed, not silently returned compressed bytes.

claim_ceiling: Iterative decompression (gzip->identity and brotli->identity, max_depth=5, try brotli then gzip) produces byte-identical output to ground-truth deterministic generate_*_body(state, target_size) on localhost buffered Python Reverse Proxy -> Mock OAuth2 server for gzip multi-chunk (chunk_size=32, compressed 95-233 bytes spanning 3-8 chunks) and gzip single-chunk (chunk_size=1024) across 4 auth states (no_auth, valid_token, expired_token, invalid_token) x 3 content types (JSON/HTML/XML) at 1KB nominal, N=10 per state per cell (240 gzip observations: 6 cells x40), plus brotli multi-chunk positive control 120/120 and identity oracle 120/120 (total 480/480), 0 silent fallbacks, 0 decompression errors, deterministic within-state grouping, seed 44, jitter 50-150ms, Python 3.12.14 stdlib gzip (default compresslevel) and brotli 1.2.0 quality6. Does NOT establish correctness on real CDN (Cloudflare/Fastly/Akamai) with Accept-Encoding negotiation, multi-layer encoding, auth-aware cache interaction, geographic latency, production concurrency; nor for larger payloads (10KB/100KB) spanning 100+ chunks, gzip compression levels 1-9, brotli quality 4-8 variation, streaming partial-frame proxy, or binary/non-1KB content. The parent unknown 'Does gzip multi-chunk correctness hold (not just brotli)?' is now established for this bounded localhost scope; remaining product gate is CDN infrastructure validation.
